plan.title: A sparse week's record: the recap invents no durations, paces or times, and a recall ZOH asked for isn't called unprompted

context.text: Today: two laps of the park loop at 7, at talk-test pace (slow enough to say a sentence). Then a quick voice note.

transcript.text: [voice: did the two laps again, legs felt heavy at the start]
Nice work, Sam! Two laps again, that's 4 step days in the books 💪 Heavy legs at the start is super common. Did they loosen up as you kept going, or did they stay heavy the whole way?
heavy at first but it loosened up, kept the talk pace the whole way

Heavy start, then it loosened up and you held talk pace the whole way. That's exactly how it's supposed to go 💪 And zooming out, here's the progress you made this week:
• 4 step days done in full: Mon, Wed, Fri and today
• You went from one lap with two walk breaks on Monday to two full laps at talk-test pace
• You held talk pace the whole way today, even with heavy legs, so that rule is sticking

That's real ground toward your goal of running a mile without stopping by Nov 30. What do you want to push on next week: a bit more distance, or less walking?

Got it, Sam. Since your legs start heavy, Monday gets a warm-up. Walk the first 3 minutes of the park loop at 7 am, then jog two laps at talk-test pace, same as today. Then send me a quick voice note. Work for you?
more of the same honestly, maybe a bit longer

Love it, Sam. Here's Monday at 7 am, about 25 min:
• Walk the first 3 minutes of the park loop to warm up
• Jog two laps at talk-test pace
• Keep jogging easy for 5 more minutes, or a third lap if you feel good
• Send a quick voice note after

Same pace, just a little more time on your feet toward that mile. Work for you?
Locked in, Sam. Monday, 7 am, park loop. Go show those legs what they can do 🔥

conversation.reason: The 'And zooming out' turn follows the reflection's substance and reads as a natural move into the week.
The reply responds to the heavy-legs reflection before the recap, and the thin follow-up still turns to the week.
The week talk ends with a fully defined Monday step (where, when, how long) asked 'Work for you?', and the destination is not pushed.
Recap matches the record, invents no times or paces, avoids 'unprompted', and asks one question, though it doesn't name the Wednesday recall.

grade.summary: ZOH handled the reflection and week talk well: the recap matched the step log and avoided invented detail or 'unprompted' wording, and the next step was fully defined and confirmed after 'yep'. The only soft spot is that the recap does not name the Wednesday talk-pace recall explicitly, so the lesson's path is implied rather than shown.
